content.title: Levi's brings $300 jeans to more stores on premium denim demand
content.summary:
STORY: Iconic American jeans maker Levi Strauss - whose rugged legacy stretches back to the late 1800s - is doubling down on high-end denim. 

The company on Tuesday told Reuters it will sell its new line of $300 Blue Tab jeans in more stores next year as it looks to broaden the Levi's brand and attract more women.

Launched in Asia earlier this year, and in around two dozen stores in Europe and the U.S. since September, Levi's Blue Tab line was inspired by heavier and stiffer Japanese selvedge denim.

In Europe, Blue Tab jeans sell for as much as 350 euros, or $410, compared with the company's traditional Red Tab jeans which top out at 130 euros, or $150.

The Blue Tab expansion comes as Levi's faces a delicate balance to cater to both budget and premium markets.

In the U.S., higher-income families riding stock market gains continue to spend freely on luxury items, in sharp contrast to the bargain hunting among lower-income shoppers.

Levi's said that while premium denim accounts for about 10% of the roughly $100 billion global denim market, it is growing faster than the regular jeans category.

Levi's also said it's expecting a strong holiday season, and added that it will limit discounts amid solid demand.
